name: יִתְרְעָם
gloss: abundance of the people; or the kinsman excels
summary: David's sixth son, born in Hebron to Eglah, David's wife (2Sa 3:5; 1Ch 3:3). The name joins יֶתֶר “abundance, pre-eminence” with עָם “people”, or the older sense “kinsman” that עָם has in names; scripture does not explain it.

evidence.note: “The sixth, יִתְרְעָם, by Eglah, David's wife; these were born to David in Hebron.”
“The sixth, יִתְרְעָם, by Eglah his wife.”
The noun יֶתֶר, “pre-eminence”, the first part of the name.

note: Takes j.ef.ar (2 tokens; BDB tags it n.m.). Whether עָם is “people” or “kinsman” here, and whether יִתְר־ is the noun or a verb form, is a reading of the form only.
